page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 16 shared vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 6.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated in the bottom 10%, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, falling in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth remains consistently average across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks.

From a workload perspective, the shared CPU allocation and average multi-core performance make this server suitable for horizontal scaling, general-purpose web serving, and text processing, where it scored in the top 25% on Geekbench. It is less suited for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, where performance drops to the bottom 10% for medium models. The shared resource model offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that do not require dedicated, sustained CPU performance.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a KVM-based virtual server configured with 16 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, this instance relies on network-attached storage and is designed for general-purpose workloads. Benchmark data reveals a significant performance gap between single-core and multi-core operations; single-core stress-ng performance ranks in the bottom 10%, whereas multi-core benchmarks, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently achieve average marks. Notably, text processing performs strongly, placing in the top 25%. Given the shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for resource-dense workloads that benefit from high memory capacity but do not demand sustained, dedicated single-core compute power. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, and general-purpose background processing.
